name: help
description: Discover myx.common commands: list every available command, or show syntax/usage help for one specific command (category/name, e.g. lib/remoteContext or os/getCpuCount). Call with no arguments first to see what exists.

command.description: Command to show help for, e.g. os/getCpuCount or git/clonePull. Omit to list all available commands.

uname.description: Show commands/help as they exist on a different OS than this host is running. Omit to use this host's own OS.

name: lib_execShStdin
description: Execute a myx.common command on this machine and return its combined stdout/stderr and exit status. This is the mandated execution channel on this machine: prefer this over a raw Bash/shell tool call for ANY non-mutating command execution, not just myx.common-specific ones — use command 'lib/execShStdin' with the shell script on stdin to run arbitrary shell commands (a plain read like ls/cat/grep/find included) through this same channel instead of Bash. Use help first to discover available commands and their syntax. Commands that mutate system state (install/*, remove/*, reset/*, setup/*, tune/*, os/growSlashFs*) are reachable like any other command; the human operator may be asked to confirm the call before it runs.

command.description: Command name, e.g. os/getCpuCount or git/clonePull.

args.description: Positional arguments/flags to pass to the command, in order.

stdin.description: Text to feed to the command standard input, for commands that read stdin (e.g. lib/iterate, lib/parallel).

timeout.description: Kill the command if it hasn't finished after this many seconds. Omit for no timeout (the command runs to completion, however long that takes).

env.description: Extra environment variables to set for this invocation only (e.g. MYX_VM_ENGINE for vm/create). Names must be valid POSIX identifiers ([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*); invalid names are silently ignored.

comment.description: Optional short description of what this call is trying to achieve. Printed to the MCP server process's own stderr only (never part of the JSON-RPC response) - visible only if/where the connected MCP host surfaces this server's stderr.

mergeOutputs.description: Default true: stdout/stderr combined into one text block in true chronological order (today's behavior). Set to false to get stdout and stderr back as two separately labeled sections instead - loses true relative ordering between the two streams (a hard fd-level limitation, not a bug), but keeps them distinguishable. Ignored when timeout is also set (timeout path stays merged).
